topic: A negritude brasileira está sendo tratada como sujeito político ou apenas como eleitorado, nas campanhas de 2026? Revista Raça Brasil
insights: The Brazilian negritude is increasingly recognized as a political subject in the 2026 campaigns, emphasizing rights and representation beyond mere voting.
The Tribunal Superior Eleitoral has mandated that at least 30% of electoral funds be allocated to black candidates, reflecting a commitment to enhance representation.
Candidates are required to self-declare their race, which influences the distribution of public campaign resources.
The political discourse is shifting to view citizens as collective subjects of rights, including various marginalized groups.
The outcome of the 2026 elections is seen as pivotal for the future of public policies aimed at combating racism and promoting racial equality.

summary: The Brazilian negritude is being increasingly recognized as a political entity in the 2026 electoral campaigns, moving beyond traditional roles as mere voters. This shift is marked by new regulations ensuring financial support for black candidates and a broader discourse on collective rights.
